What we lend against

The diamonds we lend against

We lend against diamonds worth keeping — certified investment-grade stones, engagement and dress rings, and fine diamond jewellery. A certificate helps the valuation, but an uncertified stone can still be valued and lent against.

Certified loose diamonds

GIA, IGI or HRD-certified stones, valued on the 4Cs against current market prices for that grade.

Engagement & diamond rings

Solitaires and multi-stone rings — the stone, the setting and the maker all considered.

Diamond jewellery

Necklaces, pendants, earrings and suites, including signed and period pieces.

Uncertified & older stones

No certificate is no barrier — our specialists grade and value the stone on its own merit.

How it works

Four steps. Your diamond back at the end.

Step 01

Tell us about your diamond

Send the carat, the certificate details if you have them, and a few photos. A specialist values it and sends an indicative offer the same day.

Step 02

Send it to us, insured

We arrange free, fully insured delivery, or you can bring it to our City of London office by appointment. It’s insured from the moment it leaves your hands.

Step 03

Accept the offer and get paid

Once we’ve examined the diamond in person we confirm the valuation. Accept, and the money is with you within 24 hours.

Step 04

Repay, and it comes back to you

Loans run for six months and can be extended. Repay early and you pay less, with no penalty. Your diamond is returned exactly as you left it.

Read the process in full, including what happens at the end of the term →

How we value diamonds

Valued by diamond specialists, on the 4Cs

Every diamond is assessed by a specialist — carat, cut, colour and clarity, the certificate where there is one, and, for set pieces, the mount and maker — then valued against current market prices for that grade. We don’t weigh and average, and we don’t treat a fine stone as scrap. Our specialists come from the auction houses and the trade.

Graded on the 4Cs

Carat, cut, colour and clarity, assessed by a specialist.

Certificate read and factored in

GIA, IGI or HRD — helpful, not required.

Set stones valued whole

The mount, maker and any secondary stones all counted.

Nothing sight-unseen

You see the valuation before you commit to anything.

Why Trinity rather than the high street

A pawnbroker for diamonds you intend to keep.

We-buy-diamonds and cash-for-diamonds services buy your stone outright. We don’t. A pawn loan is a loan: you keep ownership, we keep it safe, and you take it back when you repay. That difference is the whole business.
